questions.prompt: Why is the small intestine of a herbivore longer than that of a carnivore?

questions.explain: A longer gut gives more time.

questions.prompt: In an enzyme experiment, starch took 60 s to disappear at 20 °C and 20 s at 37 °C. How many times faster was the reaction at 37 °C?
Explain how the structure of the small intestine is adapted for absorbing food.
questions.modelAnswer: The small intestine is very long and its inner wall has millions of finger-like villi (with microvilli), giving an enormous surface area. The villi have thin walls, one cell thick, so digested food diffuses quickly. Each villus has a rich network of blood capillaries (and a lacteal for fats) that carries food away, keeping a steep concentration gradient.
